head: A castle near Paris.
Rooms sat empty.
slides.sub: How Disney's European park nearly failed, then found its feet.

image.label: A fairy-tale castle under grey skies with an empty plaza
image.brief: 흐린 하늘 아래 동화 같은 성과 텅 빈 광장. 1990년대 초 프랑스 교외 분위기. 실제 디즈니 성 디자인과 로고는 따라 하지 않음.

head: Tokyo was a hit.
Europe looked easy.
body: Disney's park in Tokyo was a big success, so a park near Paris seemed like a safe next step. Millions of Europeans lived a short trip away.
Euro Disney opened in April 1992 in Marne-la-Vallée, east of Paris, built largely in the American style.

image.label: A map of Europe with travel lines pointing to Paris
image.brief: 파리를 향해 선이 모이는 유럽 지도 그래픽. 1990년대 초 여행 포스터 느낌.

slides.label: hotels opened on day one, with thousands of rooms
body: The plan counted on long stays and big spending on rooms, food and souvenirs. Many visitors came for a day, spent less than hoped, and went home to Paris at night.

image.label: A long hotel corridor with closed doors
image.brief: 닫힌 문이 끝없이 이어진 호텔 복도. 조용하고 쓸쓸한 조명.

head: Critics were loud.
Some called it a disaster.
body: French intellectuals saw the park as an American invasion. One theatre director famously called it a "cultural Chernobyl."
Staff also pushed back on strict American rules about looks and grooming.

image.label: Newspapers with angry headlines on a Paris café table
image.brief: 파리 카페 테이블 위 성난 헤드라인의 신문들. 실제 신문 제호나 로고 없음.

slides.label: glasses of wine sold inside the park at opening
body: Disney kept its no-alcohol rule from the US. In France, a lunch without wine felt strange to many guests. The rule was dropped in 1993.

image.label: An empty wine glass on a park restaurant table
image.brief: 테마파크 식당 테이블 위 빈 와인잔. 뒤로 흐릿한 놀이공원 풍경.

head: Built for Americans.
Visited by Europeans.
body: Reportedly, hotels planned for light breakfasts, then guests asked for full meals. Restaurants expected people to graze all day, but many wanted to sit down for lunch at the same time.
Queues grew. Costs and debts grew faster.

image.label: A crowded restaurant at noon with long queues
image.brief: 정오에 줄이 길게 늘어선 붐비는 식당. 지친 가족들.

head: Losses pile up.
What do you do?
body: It's 1994. The park is heavily in debt, attendance is below hopes, and lenders want a plan.

options.text: Restructure the debt, cut prices and adapt to European habits
options.feedback: It means admitting the original plan was wrong and giving up income for years. Keep swiping.

options.text: Hold prices and wait for the brand to win people over
options.feedback: Disney's brand was strong, but the debt payments wouldn't wait. Keep swiping.

options.text: Walk away and let the lenders take the park
options.feedback: Disney reportedly raised the threat of closure in talks. Actually leaving would have hurt its name across Europe. Keep swiping.

image.label: Executives around a table covered in financial papers
image.brief: 재무 서류가 가득한 회의 테이블에 둘러앉은 경영진 실루엣. 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: A rescue deal.
And a new name.
body: In 1994, Disney and the banks agreed a rescue. Disney paused its royalties and fees for several years, and Saudi investor Prince Alwaleed bin Talal bought a large stake.
The resort was renamed Disneyland Paris, tying it to a city people loved.

image.label: A signature on a contract beside a pen
image.brief: 펜과 함께 서명되는 계약서 클로즈업. 1990년대 사무실 톤.

head: Lower prices.
A ride inspired by Verne.
body: Ticket and hotel prices came down, wine went on menus, and food fit local habits. In 1995, Space Mountain opened, themed on Jules Verne's journey to the Moon.
That year, the company reported its first annual profit.

image.label: A retro rocket ride lit up at night
image.brief: 밤에 불 밝힌 레트로풍 로켓 놀이기구. 19세기 공상과학 분위기. 실제 놀이기구 디자인은 따라 하지 않음.

head: What works at home
can fail abroad.
body: Disney copied a formula that worked in the US and Japan, and assumed guests would act the same way. Heavy debt left little room to learn slowly.
The comeback began when the company listened to how Europeans actually ate, spent and travelled, and fixed its finances.

image.label: Two puzzle pieces from different sets that don't fit
image.brief: 서로 다른 퍼즐에서 온 두 조각이 맞지 않는 모습. 미니멀 그래픽.

head: Test your habits
before you export them.
body: A model that wins in one market rests on assumptions about how people live. New customers may not share them.
**Try it today:** list three things your business assumes about customers. Which would change in a new city or segment?

image.label: A lit castle at dusk with a busy crowd
image.brief: 해 질 녘 불 밝힌 성 앞을 가득 메운 인파. 실제 로고와 성 디자인 없음.

factChecks.note: 개장일(1992년 4월 12일)과 위치(파리 동쪽 마른라발레)는 Disneyland Paris 공식 연혁 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1992년 4월 12일 개장 확인.
개장 시 호텔 6곳(객실 약 5,200실)은 당시 보도와 Euro Disney 자료 기준입니다. 카드에는 호텔 수 "6"만 숫자로 쓰고 객실 수는 "thousands of rooms"로만 적었습니다.
연출가 Ariane Mnouchkine의 "cultural Chernobyl" 발언은 1992년 여러 언론에 널리 인용됐습니다. 원 보도로 표현을 확인하세요.
테마파크 내 주류(와인) 판매 금지와 1993년 정책 변경은 당시 보도(NYT 등) 기준입니다. 변경 시점(1993년 6월 무렵)은 확인 후 필요하면 추가하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 개장 시 주류 금지와 이후 해제 확인. 1993년 시점은 이번 검색에서 미확인.
아침 식사 수요를 과소평가한 일, 점심시간 식당 혼잡 등은 디즈니 경영진 회고와 경영 사례로 전해지는 이야기입니다. 카드에 "reportedly"로 표시했습니다.

1994년 재무 구조조정(은행·디즈니 합의, 로열티·수수료 일시 면제, Alwaleed bin Talal 왕자 지분 투자)은 당시 Reuters, NYT, FT 보도로 확인하세요. 손실액은 자료마다 달라 숫자를 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1994년 부채 10억 달러 감축, 이자 24개월 유예 등 재무 구조조정 확인. Alwaleed 지분은 이번 검색에서 미확인.
1994년 Disneyland Paris로 개명, 1995년 Space Mountain 개장, 1995 회계연도 첫 순이익 발표는 회사 발표 기준입니다. 이익 규모는 넣지 않았습니다.
